successCriteria.description: `countLeaveDays(startDate, endDate)` returns `endDate - startDate + 1` (inclusive, calendar days, no weekend/holiday exclusion) and is the single exported helper in `leave.model.ts` — every day-count call site in the service imports and uses it, never inlining the arithmetic.

`submit(dto)` validates `startDate < endDate`, looks up the active policy via `IPolicyRepository.findById(policyId)` and checks `isActive`, enforces `minimumNoticeDays` when set, computes `year = startDate.getFullYear()`, gets-or-creates a balance, reserves days via `IBalanceRepository.updateCounters` (pendingDays += days), creates a LeaveRequest with `status = PENDING`, and writes an audit record with action `CREATE` — all in one logical flow.

`approve(requestId, approverId)` fetches the request, validates `status === PENDING`, computes days via `countLeaveDays`, checks for approved overlapping requests via `findApprovedOverlapping` (throws if any exist), verifies balance sufficiency (`availableDays >= days`), commits days (`pendingDays -= days, usedDays += days`), sets `status = APPROVED, approvedBy = approverId, approvedAt = new Date()`, and writes an audit record with action `APPROVE`.

`reject(requestId, rejectorId)` fetches the request, validates `status === PENDING`, computes days via `countLeaveDays`, releases days (`pendingDays -= days`), sets `status = REJECTED`, and writes an audit record with action `REJECT`.

`cancel(requestId, employeeId)` validates `employeeId` matches `request.employeeId`. If `status === PENDING`: releases days (`pendingDays -= days`), sets `status = CANCELLED`. If `status === APPROVED`: restores days (`usedDays -= days`), sets `status = CANCELLED`. Any other status throws. Writes an audit record with action `DELETE`.
`getById(requestId)` delegates to `ILeaveRequestRepository.findById` and returns the result; `query(params)` delegates to `ILeaveRequestRepository.findByEmployee` with the query params.

Every mutating operation (submit, approve, reject, cancel) that changes a LeaveRequest status AND balance counters AND writes an audit record must run all three through the same transaction — a failure in any step rolls back the entire operation.

constraints: LeaveService constructor takes four repository interfaces directly: `ILeaveRequestRepository`, `IBalanceRepository`, `IAuditRepository`, `IPolicyRepository` — not services. The leave service calls `IBalanceRepository.updateCounters` directly for counter mutations rather than going through `IBalanceService`.

The `submit` method resolves the policy via `IPolicyRepository.findById(policyId)` (since `CreateLeaveRequestDto` carries `policyId`, not `leaveType`) and validates `isActive === true`. It does NOT use `findActiveByLeaveType`.
No counter may go negative. Any balance counter transition that would take a counter below zero must throw an Error — never clamp or silently ignore.

All imports in the leave module must use `baseUrl`-based non-relative paths (e.g. `'shared/types'`, `'modules/balance/balance.repository.interface'`), consistent with `tsconfig.json` `baseUrl: "./src"` and all existing modules.
outOfScope: Concrete Knex/PostgreSQL repository implementations — the routes file uses stub/mock repositories; real implementations come in a later phase.
RBAC enforcement on routes (requireRole guards) — deferred to a later phase; this phase's routes accept identity parameters (approverId, employeeId) in the request body.

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle: created with `status = PENDING` (no DRAFT state in this phase). Valid transitions: PENDING → APPROVED (approve), PENDING → REJECTED (reject), PENDING → CANCELLED (cancel), APPROVED → CANCELLED (cancel). Terminal states: REJECTED, CANCELLED. No other transitions are valid — attempting one must throw.
`startDate` must be strictly before `endDate` (`startDate < endDate`). A request where `startDate >= endDate` is invalid and must be rejected at submission.
No two APPROVED LeaveRequests for the same employee may have overlapping `[startDate, endDate]` ranges. Overlap is enforced at approval time only, not at submission.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws if: startDate >= endDate, no active policy found for policyId, minimumNoticeDays not met, balance reservation would exceed available days. Must audit with action CREATE on success.
Throws if: request not found, status is not PENDING. Must audit with action REJECT on success.
Throws if: request not found, employeeId does not match request.employeeId, status is neither PENDING nor APPROVED. Must audit with action DELETE on success.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: LeaveRequest.status must use the `LeaveStatus` enum from `shared/types` — values are `DRAFT`, `PENDING`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, `CANCELLED`. The `PENDING` value (not `SUBMITTED`) is authoritative per the reconciled architecture.

LeaveBalance counters follow the three-counter model: `entitlementDays`, `usedDays`, `pendingDays`. Available days are always derived as `entitlementDays - usedDays - pendingDays`. The leave service must call `IBalanceRepository.updateCounters` with absolute counter values — never compute deltas inline.

Audit records written by the leave service must use the `AuditAction` enum (`CREATE`, `APPROVE`, `REJECT`, `DELETE`) and the `IAuditRepository.create` signature: `Omit<AuditRecord, 'id' | 'createdAt'>`. The `performedAt` field must be set to `new Date()` at the call site.

The `year` field on LeaveBalance is a plain integer (e.g. 2026) representing the calendar year, derived from `startDate.getFullYear()`. A request whose range crosses 31 December is charged in full to the year of its `startDate` — never split.

Route registration must follow the `uptime.routes.ts` pattern: export an async function `(fastify: FastifyInstance) => Promise<void>`, register routes via `fastify.get`/`fastify.post`, wrap each handler body in try/catch returning 500 on error.

integrationPoints.why: LeaveService calls `findByEmployeePolicyAndYear` for balance lookups, `getOrCreateForYear` for balance initialization, and `updateCounters` for all counter mutations (reserve, commit, release, restore).
LeaveService calls `findById` to resolve the policy from `CreateLeaveRequestDto.policyId` and validate `isActive` during submit.
LeaveService calls `create` to write an audit record for every mutating operation (submit→CREATE, approve→APPROVE, reject→REJECT, cancel→DELETE).
